messages.subject: Stop graying screen out when server is unreachable
messages.subject_clean: Stop graying screen out when server is unreachable
messages.body_plain:
Hi Folks,

I have a Shiny app that I'm using on a big monitor at my company to display some key business metrics. Occasionally, the server becomes unreachable and the app grays out. This can happen for a variety of reasons, which we can usually root-cause and fix, but in the meantime, it looks awful to see the big gray screen. We have other monitoring in place to detect these situations, so we don't get any value in having the screen go gray. My question is this, is there an override to prevent the app from restyling itself during a connection failure?

Thanks!
Adam

messages.subject: Using Shiny widgets to control Javascript?
messages.subject_clean: Using Shiny widgets to control Javascript?
messages.body_plain:
I'm working with rgl's WebGL output, and I'd like to use Shiny widgets to control the display.  Because rgl writes out so much code for each scene, the display is quite sluggish in response to changes requested by the user via widgets.  I'm looking into different approaches to fix this.

The simplest approach might be to work entirely in Javascript within the user's browser.  I would write some Javascript code that gets called when the widget is changed, and it tells the rest of the WebGL code what to do.  The reason I want to involve Shiny here is that I'd like some widgets to work this way, while others will need to talk to the server to do some more extensive computing.  I want all the widgets to look the same.

A more complicated approach could be to make custom widgets that just change part of the web page, without requiring the whole thing to be replaced.  I think this is the way the more extensive changes should be done, but there will be a delay for the round-trip to the server even if not much is being sent.

The goal is to make responses to Shiny widgets as quick as purely local changes, e.g. scene rotation.  Are there examples like this out there?

messages.subject: Re: zoom, pan, and axis rescale
messages.subject_clean: zoom, pan, and axis rescale
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

So R Shiny definitely has the low level framework, but higher level implementations remain a key barrier.
Rbokeh with htmlwidgets sounds very close (https://github.com/bokeh/rbokeh/issues/25) to providing a higher level interface that nails my original question (see the examples here: https://github.com/ramnathv/rbokeh).
But what about 3d scatter and surface plots?
ShinyRGL and threejs (http://www.htmlwidgets.org/showcase_threejs.html) provide rudimentary 3D rotate and scale, but lack real combined pan and zoom like plot.ly <http://plot.ly> (https://plot.ly/r/3d-scatter-plots/). Are there any more capable 3D plotting open source tools for shiny out there, or at least in the works?
It seems like just a matter of time, but not quite there yet...

Jonathan

messages.body_plain:
The svgPanZoom  <https://github.com/timelyportfolio/svgPanZoom>works great for me. Here's an example (I don't think you actually need SVGAnnotation to run it). Though one bug that came up for me is setting the linetype to blank in stat_density2d causes an error.

library(shiny)
library(SVGAnnotation)
library(svgPanZoom)
library(ggplot2)

ui <- shinyUI(bootstrapPage(

  svgPanZoomOutput(outputId = "main_plot")

))

server = shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$main_plot <- renderSvgPanZoom({
    p <- ggplot() + geom_point(data=data.frame(faithful),aes(x=eruptions,y=waiting)) + stat_density2d(data=data.frame(faithful),aes(x=eruptions,y=waiting, alpha =..level..),geom="poly
 gon") + scale_alpha_continuous(range=c(0.05,0.2))
    svgPanZoom(p, controlIconsEnabled = T)
  })
})

runApp(list(ui=ui,server=server))

messages.subject_clean: Developing Shiny Apps with Multiple Monitors

One way to do this is using shiny server.  Shiny server can reload the app after changes.  You can develop using rstudio in the shiny server directory and changes will be available in another browser window running the shiny app.

Sean

messages.body_plain:
inputdata <- reactive({
    switch(input$dataset,
          "file" = filenames)
  })

should just be:

inputdata <- reactive({
  if (grepl("[/\\\\]", input$dataset)) {
    stop("Invalid dataset")
  }
  read.csv(file.path("data", input$dataset))
})

This assumes that your CSV files are in a "data" subdirectory of your app, which I highly recommend. Also note that I ensure input$dataset doesn't include / or \ character, using grepl. This is because a hacker could put whatever value into input$dataset, such as a path that starts with "../../" or whatever; by ensuring that no path separators are in the input, you should be safe to open whatever's in the data directory by that name.

> >

On Monday, February 16, 2015 at 8:30:00 AM UTC+1, Jamie M. Kass wrote:
> Not sure what's wrong, but I cannot seem to select multiple files even when selecting multiple =TRUE for fileInput(). I am on Mac OS Yosemite and running the app on the latest RStudio. Has anyone else experienced this problem recently?
>
> On Wednesday, 3 April 2013 17:48:21 UTC-4, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > If you want them to upload two separate files in order, then probably the easiest/best way to do that is to include two separate fileInput fields. This will let them change the file if they get it wrong.
> >
> > In general though, when you upload multiple files through fileInput, then input$file1 (in your case) will be a dataframe where each row is a different file. So to retrieve the first file's datapath it would be input$file1[[1, 'datapath']] and for the second, input$file1[[2, 'datapath']].

> >

> > > Here is what I have so far (which doesn't work).  Any advice would be appreciated!
> > >
> > > ui.R
> > > shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
> > >
> > >   # title
> > >   headerPanel("Update bee data with species IDs"),
> > >
> > >   sidebarPanel(
> > >     fileInput('file1', 'First upload the raw bee data, then upload the species info',

> > > ))

the RData file, otherwise it will surely trigger an error if you have
not uploaded the file yet (essentially load(NULL)). You may want to
read this article: http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/validation.html

Regards,

           "INDIAN" = as.character(INDIAN),

messages.subject: Re: DT::DataTable how to combine extension?
messages.subject_clean: DT::DataTable how to combine extension?
messages.body_plain:
Yes, it is possible to combine extensions, as the DT website has
clearly indicated in beginning of the page:
http://rstudio.github.io/DT/extensions.html. In theory, this is what
you want to do:

m = as.data.frame(round(matrix(rnorm(10000), 100), 5))
m = cbind(ID = seq_len(nrow(m)), m)
library(DT)
datatable(m, extensions = c('Scroller', 'FixedColumns'), options = list(
  deferRender = TRUE,
  dom = "frtiS",
  scrollY = 200,
  scrollCollapse = TRUE
))

However, I think there is a conflict (or bug) between Scroller and
FixedColumns. In the above example, only the table header ID is fixed,
and the cells in the ID column are not. I think you need to ask the
DataTables developers to fix it.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: publish shiny App on my own Linux server with a custom URL
messages.subject_clean: publish shiny App on my own Linux server with a custom URL
messages.body_plain:
OK, let's take a step back.

You have both Apache and Shiny Server configured to listen on port 80. That is certainly not going to work. I think the first question is whether you actually need Apache for anything. The simplest would be to shut down Apache (or configure it to stop listening on port 80, and reload) and restart Shiny Server, and I think that should start working.

If you do need to have Apache listening on port 80 (for example if you have other web stuff you are serving using other URL paths on the same host/port) then what you want to do is not serve up a <Directory>, but rather, proxy that traffic through to Shiny Server. To do this, change Shiny Server back to listening on port 3838 and remove the server_name directive, then set ProxyPass <http://httpd.apache.org/docs/current/mod/mod_proxy.html#proxypass> and ProxyPassReverse <http://httpd.apache.org/docs/current/mod/mod_proxy.html#proxypassreverse> directives in your Apache config. Probably something like this:

ProxyPass / http://127.0.0.1:3838/
ProxyPassReverse / http://127.0.0.1:3838/

If that doesn't work, first try viewing port 3838 from inside the firewall to see if the Shiny Server instance is even working. If that works, then check the Apache logs to see why the proxying is failing.

messages.body_plain:
I am glad to announce that shinyData is now out of beta testing and has a stable version 0.1.1 <https://github.com/yindeng/shinyData>. Feel free to check it out.

On Friday, January 23, 2015 at 4:54:49 PM UTC-8, Yindeng Jiang wrote:
> Shiny is a fantastic framework for building interactive and powerful applications. For the past few months I've been working on an app called shinyData to make it easy to perform common data analysis tasks (usually referred to as business intelligence). It's available on GitHub <https://github.com/yindeng/shinyData>, and it's also hosted at ShinyApps.io <https://roose.shinyapps.io/shinyData/>. Part of shinyData is essentially a front end to ggplot2 (you can read more about this aspect at my blog post here <https://shinydata.wordpress.com/2015/01/08/front-end-for-ggplot2/>), but it's intended to be much more than that. In a nutshell, what I envision to achieve is to integrate the features already available in various r packages to create an end-to-end solution to users who may or may not know r. All feedback are welcome.
>

messages.body_plain:
Hei,
  Remember always paste your source code here, so others know what are you talking and debug it.
  If I understand correctly, I thought you mixed the 'value' and 'text' of a selectInput box.

  suppose you have a select input as follow:

selectInput("myCSV", "Select CSV data:",
            c("dat1.csv", "dat2.csv"))

If you didn't specify names for your option, the default names are their values, if you don't want to show the extension, you can give each value a name:
selectInput("myCSV", "Select CSV data:",
            c("A" = "dat1.csv", "dat2" = "dat2.csv"))

Hope this helpful to you.

messages.subject: renderTable Caption problems
messages.subject_clean: renderTable Caption problems
messages.body_plain:
I was attempting to add captions to an html table created via renderTable.  While renderTable didn't have a caption argument, I saw that it passed additional arguments to xtable (which did have a caption argument).

I attempted to use this and received a partial matching error. While there aren't other arguments in xtable starting with "caption", the renderTable() function was also passing the additional arguments to print.xtable (which had arguments caption.placement and caption.width).

I got around this by specifying the values for both caption.placement and caption.width, but is there a way to get around it without having to do that? Is there a better way to add a table title/header within Shiny? A minimal code example is below and here <https://gist.github.com/cmishra/87bad81d4eed495272ae>:

library(shiny)

serverShouldWork <- function(input, output) {
  output$bTable <- renderTable({iris}, caption=paste("test"),
    caption.placement = getOption("xtable.caption.placement", "top"),
    caption.width = getOption("xtable.caption.width", NULL)
  )
}

serverDoesWork <- function(input, output) {
  output$bTable <- renderTable({iris}, caption="test")
}

ui <- fluidPage("RenderTable Example",
  tableOutput("bTable") #table of information on beds (beds)
)

app1 <- shinyApp(ui, serverDoesWork)
app2 <- shinyApp(ui, serverShouldWork)

runApp(app1)
runApp(app2)

I apologize if there is something obvious that I've overlooked, I've learned R an isolated, need-to-do manner (so don't know many simple things), and this is my first real development experience with Shiny.

Any other alternative for the same is most welcome.

Please help me..I am new to shiny

Thanx

messages.subject: Re: after new r release shiny account needs payment

messages.body_plain:
Yoni,

You should have received email from RStudio regarding shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>'s end of beta testing period (March 6th). After this date you either need to upgrade your account to a paid plan for extra features, or stick with the free plan which has limited functionalities. Please refer to http://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps/ for list of plans and differences.

In your case it seems that you have crossed the max limits of free plan. You could have more than 5 active applications, or you have a private (authorized) application, or some other limitation of free plan.

I have CCed shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> forum on this email, but in future you can post to that discussion group for faster response:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/shinyapps-users

Best,
Fereshteh

messages.subject: updateNumericInput takes one cycle to update, where updateSliderInput takes two!!!
messages.subject_clean: updateNumericInput takes one cycle to update, where updateSliderInput takes two!!!
messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone,

I have been dealing with a really frustrating issue that I cannot seem to resolve.  I have read everything I could find on the topic – including these boards – and there does not seem to be any good explanations as to what is happening underneath the R code in order to help inform where I should go from here. I have limited javascript knowledge, so I am aware the answers might be staring me in the face.

I have ten pairs of dual reactive (or bi-directional) widgets, and the pairs consist of a numeric and slider field that reflects the same value.  My application has a rather complex system that updates either of the two necessary widgets to whatever value was most recently modified in the user interface.  This update occurs after a preset period has passed of no subsequent user modifications.  The dependent reactive functions, which render my plots, are triggered by the user updated numeric fields’ values, not the sliders.  The actual widget update commands are carried out within a function inside of an observe block.

Side note from http://www.inside-r.org/packages/cran/shiny/docs/updateNumericInput:  For update functions, “The messages are collected and sent after all the observers (including outputs) have finished running.”  Is there a name for this, because it is not called “console flush?”  For the purposes of this thread, I am going to call it, a “cycle”; therefore a “cycle” will be defined as when server decides all of its reactions and observers are complete, and it is time to send information back to the UI.  I would love to know the true technical name for this.

My big issue is just after a “cycle” when both the updateNumericInput() and updateSliderInput() functions are executed with the same value, and all the graphs have been updated on the UI.  The next cycle’s initial observe function (i.e. the observe function that triggers all other reactions), takes in both the input$numtxt and input$slider values, however, the numtxt is the correct (just updated) value, and the slider is the previous (not updated) value.  To reiterate, this happens even if both fields received an update (e.g. due to the numtxt field being out of bounds, or NA).

The strange thing is, after the subsequent cycle finishes running, the next cycle (after the previous broken cycle) takes in the correct value regardless if the slider was updated a second time due to a complete rerun.  I thought for a moment that there was an issue with a delay.  That is, that it took a second for the UI to be ready to tell the server its value was updated, but I ruled that out.  I am currently using a workaround where the initial observe function executes one extra time after every completed cycle making absolutely no invalidations or resumes() in its descendants.  This brief extra cycle seems to be enough for the input$slider value to be the correct updated value.  Just to be thorough I used the bug tracker feature to watch the exact values going to into the updateSliderInput() function, and everything exactly as it should, and is exactly like the values going into the updateNumericInput() function.

Does anyone have any insights as to what is happening here, where I might have gone wrong, and/or what I should read to get a great understanding?  One of the things I wanted to figure out was exactly what information the server is sending out in the output.  I tried for some time to get to get a profile of the input and output information and print([info]) ; flush.console() it so I can see it pre-cycle.  It seems the information entering the session by way of the session$sendInputMessage() function is not readable, and if it is I would love to know how.

Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Thanks,

Reino

P.S. If I get some support through these boards, I will be glad to keep this thread up-to-date with what I learn on the topic.

P.P.S. I never using a "." character in any of my variable names.

messages.subject: Re: updateNumericInput takes one cycle to update, where updateSliderInput takes two!!!
messages.subject_clean: updateNumericInput takes one cycle to update, where updateSliderInput takes two!!!
messages.body_plain:
Here is an example:

ui.R
library(shiny)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Example"),
  sidebarPanel(
    numericInput("numtxt", label = h6("numtxt"),
                 min = 0, max = 100, step = 10, value = 50),

    sliderInput("slider", label = h6("slider"),
                min = 1, max = 100, value = 100)
  ),
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("distPlot")
  )
))

server.R
library(shiny)
shinyServer(function(session, input, output) {
  r_val <- reactiveValues()
  r_val[['count']] <- 0
  line_number <<- 0
  lnum <- function(){line_number <<- line_number + 1 ; paste0(line_number," ")}
  fixer_func <- function(num, slr){
    print(paste0(lnum(),"numtxt is being updated from: ", num, " to ", 50)) ; flush.console()
    updateNumericInput(session, inputId = "numtxt", value = 50)
    print(paste0(lnum(),"slider is being updated from: ", slr, " to ", 50)) ; flush.console()
    updateSliderInput(session,  inputId = "slider", value = 50)
  }
  session$onFlush(function(){print(paste0(lnum(),"#### Pre flush ####")) ; flush.console()})
  session$onFlushed(function(){print(paste0(lnum(),"#### Post flush ####")) ; flush.console()})
  observe({
    print(paste0(lnum(),"## Observe Executed ##")) ; flush.console()
    print(paste0(lnum(),"# Current Cycle Number = ", isolate(r_val[['count']]), " #"))
    numtxt <- input$numtxt
    slider <- input$slider
    print(paste0(lnum(),"# numtxt = ", numtxt, " slider = ", slider, " #")) ; flush.console()
    if( numtxt >= 50 & slider >= 50 ){
      isolate(r_val[['count']] <- r_val[['count']] + 1)
    } else{
      fixer_func(numtxt, slider)
    }
  })
  for_plots <- reactive({
    print(paste0(lnum(),"## reactive Executed ##")) ; flush.console()
    r_val[['count']]

    isolate(value <- input$numtxt + input$slider)
    print(paste0(lnum(),"# value: ", value, " #")) ; flush.console()
    return(value)
  })
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
    print(paste0(lnum(),"## renderPlot Executed ##")) ; flush.console()
    data <- for_plots()
    plot(rnorm(data), rnorm(data))
  })
})

In order to observe the behavior I am referring to in my original post just, just click on the 50 in the "numtxt" numeric entry box, and delete just the zero. The app should run immediately and spit out in the console this text:

Listening on http://XXX.X.X.X:XXXX
[1] "1 ## Observe Executed ##"
[1] "2 # Current Cycle Number = 0 #"
[1] "3 # numtxt = 50 slider = 100 #"
[1] "4 ## renderPlot Executed ##"
[1] "5 ## reactive Executed ##"
[1] "6 # value: 150 #"
[1] "7 #### Pre flush ####"
[1] "8 #### Post flush ####"
[1] "9 ## Observe Executed ##"
[1] "10 # Current Cycle Number = 1 #"
[1] "11 # numtxt = 5 slider = 100 #"
[1] "12 numtxt is being updated from: 5 to 50"
[1] "13 slider is being updated from: 100 to 50"
[1] "14 ## Observe Executed ##"
[1] "15 # Current Cycle Number = 1 #"
[1] "16 # numtxt = 50 slider = 100 #"
[1] "17 ## renderPlot Executed ##"
[1] "18 ## reactive Executed ##"
[1] "19 # value: 150 #"
[1] "20 ## Observe Executed ##"
[1] "21 # Current Cycle Number = 2 #"
[1] "22 # numtxt = 50 slider = 50 #"
[1] "23 ## renderPlot Executed ##"
[1] "24 ## reactive Executed ##"
[1] "25 # value: 100 #"

The issue I am having is that on line 13 "slider is being updated from: 100 to 50."  I have looked at this in the debugger; the slider really IS being updated to 50, however, on line 16 "# numtxt = 50 slider = 100 #", you can see that the slider is still being taken in as 100, and has not been updated. Additionally, you can see that it runs twice from lines 14 to 16, before it meets the criteria to update the plot. This should also be counted as two cycles, instead of one. It seems two when two updates take place, the observe function schedules two invalidations back to back, and one one changes at a time.

What I would love to figure out how to stop it from reexecuting like on line 20.

I have read everything I could find on the topic – including these boards – and there does not seem to be any good explanations as to what is happening underneath the R code in order to help inform where I should go from here. I have limited javascript knowledge, so I am aware the answers might be staring me in the face.
> >
> >
> >
> > I have ten pairs of dual reactive (or bi-directional) widgets, and the pairs consist of a numeric and slider field that reflects the same value.  My application has a rather complex system that updates either of the two necessary widgets to whatever value was most recently modified in the user interface.  This update occurs after a preset period has passed of no subsequent user modifications.  The dependent reactive functions, which render my plots, are triggered by the user updated numeric fields’ values, not the sliders.  The actual widget update commands are carried out within a function inside of an observe block.
> >
> >
> >
> > Side note from http://www.inside-r.org/packages/cran/shiny/docs/updateNumericInput:  For update functions, “The messages are collected and sent after all the observers (including outputs) have finished running.”  Is there a name for this, because it is not called “console flush?”  For the purposes of this thread, I am going to call it, a “cycle”; therefore a “cycle” will be defined as when server decides all of its reactions and observers are complete, and it is time to send information back to the UI.  I would love to know the true technical name for this.
> >
> >
> >
> > My big issue is just after a “cycle” when both the updateNumericInput() and updateSliderInput() functions are executed with the same value, and all the graphs have been updated on the UI.  The next cycle’s initial observe function (i.e. the observe function that triggers all other reactions), takes in both the input$numtxt and input$slider values, however, the numtxt is the correct (just updated) value, and the slider is the previous (not updated) value.  To reiterate, this happens even if both fields received an update (e.g. due to the numtxt field being out of bounds, or NA).
> >
> >
> >
> > The strange thing is, after the subsequent cycle finishes running, the next cycle (after the previous broken cycle) takes in the correct value regardless if the slider was updated a second time due to a complete rerun.  I thought for a moment that there was an issue with a delay.  That is, that it took a second for the UI to be ready to tell the server its value was updated, but I ruled that out.  I am currently using a workaround where the initial observe function executes one extra time after every completed cycle making absolutely no invalidations or resumes() in its descendants.  This brief extra cycle seems to be enough for the input$slider value to be the correct updated value.  Just to be thorough I used the bug tracker feature to watch the exact values going to into the updateSliderInput() function, and everything exactly as it should, and is exactly like the values going into the updateNumericInput() function.
> >

> >
> > Does anyone have any insights as to what is happening here, where I might have gone wrong, and/or what I should read to get a great understanding?  One of the things I wanted to figure out was exactly what information the server is sending out in the output.  I tried for some time to get to get a profile of the input and output information and print([info]) ; flush.console() it so I can see it pre-cycle.  It seems the information entering the session by way of the session$sendInputMessage() function is not readable, and if it is I would love to know how.

messages.subject: Re: updateNumericInput takes one cycle to update, where updateSliderInput takes two!!!
messages.subject_clean: updateNumericInput takes one cycle to update, where updateSliderInput takes two!!!
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the info, that made it a piece of cake to diagnose and fix!

The issue is specific to the sliderInput. The sliderInput uses a 250 millisecond debounce <http://drupalmotion.com/article/debounce-and-throttle-visual-explanation> for performance/responsiveness reasons. So the numericInput sends its new value immediately while the sliderInput waits 250ms to make sure you're not going to change the value some more.

I've got an experimental fix that you can try with:

devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny@joe/bugfix/slider-delay")

Don't forget to restart R after installing.

Also, in the future, you might find options(shiny.trace=TRUE) to be helpful; set it before running your Shiny app and Shiny will dump the messages it sends and receives to the R console. In this case I could clearly see that the updated values from each of the input controls were coming in two different messages, and with the fix they are coalesced into one.

> > > Side note from http://www.inside-r.org/packages/cran/shiny/docs/updateNumericInput:  For update functions, “The messages are collected and sent after all the observers (including outputs) have finished running.”  Is there a name for this, because it is not called “console flush?”  For the purposes of this thread, I am going to call it, a “cycle”; therefore a “cycle” will be defined as when server decides all of its reactions and observers are complete, and it is time to send information back to the UI.  I would love to know the true technical name for this.
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > My big issue is just after a “cycle” when both the updateNumericInput() and updateSliderInput() functions are executed with the same value, and all the graphs have been updated on the UI.  The next cycle’s initial observe function (i.e. the observe function that triggers all other reactions), takes in both the input$numtxt and input$slider values, however, the numtxt is the correct (just updated) value, and the slider is the previous (not updated) value.  To reiterate, this happens even if both fields received an update (e.g. due to the numtxt field being out of bounds, or NA).
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > The strange thing is, after the subsequent cycle finishes running, the next cycle (after the previous broken cycle) takes in the correct value regardless if the slider was updated a second time due to a complete rerun.  I thought for a moment that there was an issue with a delay.  That is, that it took a second for the UI to be ready to tell the server its value was updated, but I ruled that out.  I am currently using a workaround where the initial observe function executes one extra time after every completed cycle making absolutely no invalidations or resumes() in its descendants.  This brief extra cycle seems to be enough for the input$slider value to be the correct updated value.  Just to be thorough I used the bug tracker feature to watch the exact values going to into the updateSliderInput() function, and everything exactly as it should, and is exactly like the values going into the updateNumericInput() function.

messages.body_plain:
Shiny Server won't run apps as root (at least I don't think so).

If you really want to do this, you need to make sure the "shiny" user has write permissions to path-to-file. I'd encourage you to limit the write permissions to the minimal set of directories that are necessary (e.g. don't let the app itself be modified by the "shiny" user, just a specific directory where the data will live).

messages.body_plain:
Your RStudio Server runs with the permissions of your user account. Shiny Server (by default) runs as a low-privileged user named "shiny", this is because it's expected to face less trusted traffic than RStudio Server.

The permission isn't in shiny-server itself; it's on the filesystem. Can you run this command from the shell?

ls -ld path-to-data-directory

where path-to-data-directory is replaced with the directory where your data should live?

messages.body_plain:
Dear Joe,

Yes I mean reactive expressions - I see now that the output$blah stuff also renders ok.

But when I try to refer to reactive expressions, I get messages such as “not allowed outside a reactive environment”.

Here is an attempt at an example:

## function sourced or in package

AuthMenuMacro <- function(input, session, code){

  …other observe functions that update menus….

  …other output functions that output plots, data tables….

  AuthToken <- reactive({

    token <- getTokenFromCode(code)

  })

}

## server.r

code <- createAuthenticationCode()

shinyServer(function(input, output, session)){

  AuthMenuMacro(input, output, code)

  output$API_plot <- renderPlot({

    ## error as can’t see function AuthToken() within renderAuthMenu()
    data <- getAPIData(AuthToken())

    plot(data)

  })

}

A quick update as I realised I worked this one out but didn't post the answer:
- it's simply that the audio file needs to be in a 'www' subdirectory, but no need to refer to this in the 'src' filepath.
- i.e. leave the line as it is in the example below, but make sure "audio.wav" is in a "www" dir.

On Friday, 19 September 2014 11:35:25 UTC+1, Andrew Caines wrote:
> Hello All,
>

>
> In my browser, the controls render ok (therefore I know the function is recognised), but the audio is not found (i.e. nothing plays). The audio file is in the same directory as the server.R and ui.R files (and I've tried moving it to a subdir) and plays fine in general media applications. It's a WAV but I've also tried MP3. I'm using Chrome on Mac Mavericks and have also tried Firefox and Safari.
>
> Here's the line of code I'm using. Does anyone have experience of this issue, or know what could be the cause?
>
> tags$audio(src = "audio.wav", type = "audio/wav", autoplay = NA, controls = NA)
>
> many thanks, Andrew
messages.body_snippet:

messages.body_plain:
Sure. Here is a short example:

> library(shiny)
> tags$iframe(url = 'http://foo.bar.com/?a=1&b=2')
<iframe url="http://foo.bar.com/?a=1&b=2"></iframe>

You see & is escaped to &. Other special characters include ", <,
and >. If you want to construct an HTML tag, normally I'd recommend
you to use tags$ unless you are 100% sure the tag content/attributes
do not contain special characters.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
I see there are methods of invoking exit processing when a session ends (e.g. onSessionEnded), but I can't find a method for specifying exit processing with the *app* exits.

In my particular use case, I need to establish an SSH tunnel to a data source when the app starts, and tear it down when the app exits. Creating the tunnel is done in server.R, prior to the shinyServer() call (via a system() call that creates the tunnel, stores a control handle, and puts it in the background). But I can't figure out a point to specify the tear-down code when the app exits.

Any ideas?

Thanks,
Eric

messages.subject: Turn a shiny app into a desktop application?
messages.subject_clean: Turn a shiny app into a desktop application?
messages.body_plain: I have a shiny app that I'd like non-R-users can easily run on their computers. I think the easiest approach would probably be hosting the app in the cloud (like shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>) so the user only need a web browser, but that can have performance limitations (like if you need to process large data sets) and security concerns (even though can be mitigated with account permissions). Another approach would be running the app locally on the user's machine, but in order to make it as painless as possible, it would be best if the app just behaved like a regular standalone desktop application (which runs R and shiny in the background). The application would probably need to have its own browser window to run shiny. Anyone have suggestions on how to achieve this? I think the Rstudio IDE is exactly something like that (ie, a web based app that behaves like a desktop app), so I guess this approach is not totally crazy. Any idea? (even if it's a completely different approach but achieves the same goal of simplifying the user experience.)

I used Shiny to create an interface for (pseudo) batch geocoding the addresses in an uploaded spreadsheet and visualizing the results on a Leaflet map (repository here <https://github.com/emanuelfeld/geocoder> contains the relevant R scripts).

Really, I'm iterating through a list of the addresses in the file and making a Google Geocoder API call each time. Does anyone have advice/pointers on how to go about passing my address values from server.R to the javascript geocoder and the geocoded addresses back to server.R, where I render the results as a data table?

Many thanks!

Emanuel

                          method called the Marey map method introduced by A. Chakravarti in 1991 . MareyMap accepts Marey
                          map data as input (genetic and physical positions of markers for a set of chromosomes of a species) and

messages.subject: Re: Loading RData and Filling selectInput Menus
messages.subject_clean: Loading RData and Filling selectInput Menus
messages.body_plain:
You created a new environment new.env() and returned it in
loadRData(), but you did not let ls() know that environment. The
default environment that ls() uses is its calling environment; in your
case, there is basically nothing in the calling environment of ls().
You may assign the environment to a variable, e.g.

env = loadRData(input)

Then pass it to ls() explicitly, e.g. ls(env)

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: Functional pattern with Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Functional pattern with Shiny
messages.body_plain:
It's hard to say whether you're on the right track or not without more specifics. It sounds like you have this to start with:

a <- function(x) {...}
b <- function(x) {...}
c <- function(x) {...}
d <- function(x) {...}

And you're essentially calling d(c(b(a(...)))), is that right?

The reactive version of this, if you didn't want to modify the original functions, would be like this:

rA <- reactive(a(input$foo))
rB <- reactive(b(rA()))
rC <- reactive(c(rB()))
rD <- reactive(d(rC()))

Then your outputs could access any of rA, rB, rC, or rD by invoking them like a function.

Does that help?

It's hard to say whether you're on the right track or not without more specifics. It sounds like you have this to start with:

a <- function(x) {...}
b <- function(x) {...}
c <- function(x) {...}
d <- function(x) {...}

And you're essentially calling d(c(b(a(...)))), is that right?

The reactive version of this, if you didn't want to modify the original functions, would be like this:

rA <- reactive(a(input$foo))
rB <- reactive(b(rA()))
rC <- reactive(c(rB()))
rD <- reactive(d(rC()))

Then your outputs could access any of rA, rB, rC, or rD by invoking them like a function.

Does that help?

messages.body_plain:
Shiny does its work at onload time too. It's ugly, but perhaps use a setInterval to try repeatedly until Shiny.onInputChange is present. Either that, or call session$sendCustomMessage from the server when the session begins and have the custom message handler do the work you're trying to do in onload.

Ideally we would have an event for this, it's something we've considered but not acted on. Can you tell us what your use case is for executing JS at startup?

messages.subject: Re: How to access the input variable in ui.R in shiny?
messages.subject_clean: How to access the input variable in ui.R in shiny?
messages.body_plain:
It's not particularly intuitive, it requires dynamic UI (see this article <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/dynamic-ui.html>):

---

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  numericInput("count", "Number of textboxes", 3),
  hr(),
  uiOutput("textboxes")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$textboxes <- renderUI({
    if (input$count == 0)
      return(NULL)

    lapply(1:input$count, function(i) {
      id <- paste0("text", i)
      numericInput(id, NULL, value = input[[id]])
    })
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.subject: Re: Bootstrap update policy
messages.subject_clean: Bootstrap update policy
messages.body_plain:
Hi Thomas -

We don't have a specific policy for updating Bootstrap. We don't have a problem with updating Bootstrap, as long as they are bugfix releases, but we're also not committed to keeping on top of the latest version.

For the next Shiny release, I can update to the latest version of Bootstrap.

Also, we do accept pull requests. :)

-Winston

On Mon, Mar 16, 2015 at 8:06 AM, Thomas Lin Pedersen <thom...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Can the Shiny developers elaborate on how the update to newer versions of Bootstrap will happen following the bump to version 3? As Shiny is now using a version that is under active development, minor releases will occur at intervals. As I understand Bootstraps update policy all updates to version 3 should be backwards compatible so it would be easy to just bump Bootstrap to the most current version every time Shiny sees an update.
>
> My current reason for asking is that the latest version of Bootstrap includes an update to Glyphicon, containing some new icons I would like to use, but I generally see no reason why not keeping up with the Bootstrap version is a good idea. What is the thoughts from RStudio/Shiny?
>
> best Thomas

messages.subject: Re: Can't get Regex to work with renderdatatable and shiny_0.11.1
messages.subject_clean: Can't get Regex to work with renderdatatable and shiny_0.11.1
messages.body_plain:
Unfortunately DataTables does not accept per-column configurations for
detailed search options (you can only turn on/off the `searchable`
option for individual columns:
http://datatables.net/reference/option/columnDefs), and it is not
smart enough to infer from the global option regex = TRUE for
individual columns, either. Therefore it is difficult for us to
support this in shiny. You can only use regular expressions in the
global search box. Sorry.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: selectInput fails to select (always resets) with Shiny > 10.0
messages.subject_clean: selectInput fails to select (always resets) with Shiny > 10.0
messages.body_plain:
I do not know why it worked before, but it seems to me that it should
not have worked -- there is cyclic dependency in your code:

input$DepVar <- output$DepVar <- Data() <- input$DepVar

So when the select input changes, output$DepVar will be regenerated,
hence input$DepVar is regenerated as well, and because it is
regenerated without a pre-selected value, it always uses the first
value. Although it looks a little weird, you can use input$DepVar as
the pre-selected value, e.g.

  selectInput('DepVar','Dependent Variable',choices=names(Data()$df.raw),

              selected = input$DepVar,
                     selectize=FALSE)

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: Turn a shiny app into a desktop application?
messages.subject_clean: Turn a shiny app into a desktop application?
messages.body_plain:
Huidong,

I'm not sure I understand your point. So why is it crazy to run a web app entirely on a clients machine as a desktop application?

Yindeng

On Mar 16, 2015, at 4:38 AM, Huidong TIAN <tienh...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I feel it's crazy still. The idea of running it on client side is to use client CPU, but any application on cloud will use cloud's CPU.
>
>
> On Thursday, March 12, 2015 at 7:37:20 PM UTC+1, Yindeng Jiang wrote:
> > I have a shiny app that I'd like non-R-users can easily run on their computers. I think the easiest approach would probably be hosting the app in the cloud (like shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>) so the user only need a web browser, but that can have performance limitations (like if you need to process large data sets) and security concerns (even though can be mitigated with account permissions). Another approach would be running the app locally on the user's machine, but in order to make it as painless as possible, it would be best if the app just behaved like a regular standalone desktop application (which runs R and shiny in the background). The application would probably need to have its own browser window to run shiny. Anyone have suggestions on how to achieve this? I think the Rstudio IDE is exactly something like that (ie, a web based app that behaves like a desktop app), so I guess this approach is not totally crazy. Any idea? (even if it's a completely different approach but achieves the same goal of simplifying the user experience.)
>

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

Sorry for late reply. it's GMT+7 here :).
I'm thinking about integrating authentication using PHP and shiny. At the 1st time, users are required to input user and password (1st page).
After authentication success, PHP will redirect the users to another page (2nd page) with full iframe. That's where shiny is loaded.

In the 2nd page, there are 2 javascript variables defined as below:
<script type="text/javascript">
document.domain = "SERVER_HOSTNAME";
var p_un= "<?php echo $encrypted_username; ?>";
var p_token = "<?php echo $encrypted_password; ?>";
</script>
<iframe src="http://SERVER_HOSTNAME:666" frameborder="0"></iframe>

I know this leads to vulnerability, that's why I encrypt the variables. un and token will be validated in database later.
in the ui.R file, they will be sent to server at startup:
  tags$script('
          window.onload = setTimeout(function() {
            document.domain = "SERVER_HOSTNAME";
            var s_un = parent.p_un;
            var s_token = parent.p_token;
            Shiny.onInputChange("un", s_un);
            Shiny.onInputChange("token", s_token);
          },1000);
          ')

using setTimeout, the variables are read successfully in Chrome and Mozilla, but not for IE. See error below:

 <https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/-cMpq78ayEBc/VQeVgJq58kI/AAAAAAAAAZo/Xw-YHgc_9O4/s1600/Untitled2.png>
This is interesting since Not implemented only happens if I'm using iframe. If I execute shiny page directly, the code runs smoothly on all browsers. (of course I need to change s_un and s_token value to something else. E.g.: s_un = Math.random())

Any ideas ? :)

Thanks

messages.body_plain:
Encrypted or no, do not make your auth credentials accessible via JavaScript, especially in an environment like Shiny where it is so common to run third party Javascript code. The best solution is to use Shiny Server Pro where we have thought through all of these problems and solved them. If you really cannot use our commercial software then focus on an approach that protects the R process from ever even seeing unauthenticated traffic. Trying to auth after the browser has already connected to Shiny is too late.

messages.subject_clean: Another binding issue with nested uiOutput
messages.body_plain:
I've found another issue with the bindings in nested uiOutput, but I'm having a bit of trouble coming up with a simple reproducible example. Here's the gist of it, though:

Given an app with the following structure

uiOutput(
  sidebarPanel(...)
  mainPanel(
    uiOutput(...)
  )
)

As soon as an output (not an input) is created inside the inner uiOutput, it breaks some dynamically generated inputs in the sidebarPanel. However, the following structure doesn't exhibit the issue:

uiOutput(
  sidebarPanel(...)
  mainPanel(...)
)

This format comes with its own issues for me, though.

I'll keep working on an actual runnable example, but hopefully this might be enough to track down the problem.

messages.subject_clean: shiny kills app after a while
messages.body_plain:
You want to set app_idle_timeout for that app to a large number of seconds.

If your startup times are long enough you might also find that Shiny Server is giving up on the process while it's still trying to load--you can control that threshold with app_init_timeout.

Hey guys. I've been using Shiny for a very long time now, but I can't figure out a clean way to do this.

I have two selectizeInput elements. The choices in the second are computed based on the selection in the first. Think Role, Colleague - you select "Programmer", second input shows you a list of names, you select "Michael", I print you his salary.

Now here's the annoying part. The choices in the second input frequently overlap. So after you select Michael the Programmer, you decide to look up Michael from PR. PR is a one-man department, so when you select PR in the first input, the second input triggers updateSelectInput(session, "name", choices = c("Michael"))..the input is again "Michael", and an observer that is only watching the second field will not invalidate!

The way I deal with this currently is by checking if the current choice is the same as the one I'm updating to, and adding whitespace to the new value to differentiate it if so. I've tried several more beautiful hacks in an attempt to invalidate the input when updating to it, but this is the simplest one that still worked. Can we just do observer::flush or something?

messages.subject: Re: Remove selectInput Variable Once Chosen
messages.subject_clean: Remove selectInput Variable Once Chosen
messages.body_plain:
I wonder whether it'd be better to just have selectInput(multiple=TRUE) and use that as-is; it's not possible to choose the same item twice at a given moment.

However, if you want to do literally as you described, this is an example of how you'd do it:

--

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("letters", "Choose letter(s)", LETTERS,
        multiple = TRUE),
      actionButton("choose", "Choose")
    ),
    mainPanel(
      verbatimTextOutput("list")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # v$choices will represent the values that have been chosen
  v <- reactiveValues(choices = c())

  # When the Choose button is clicked, add the current letters to v$choices
  # and update the selector
  observeEvent(input$choose, {
    v$choices <- append(v$choices, input$letters)
    updateSelectInput(session, "letters",
      choices = LETTERS[!(LETTERS %in% v$choices)]
    )
  })

  output$list <- renderPrint({
    v$choices
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.body_plain:
Two thoughts:

1) When you call updateSelectInput, it seems like you should also be passing value="" to clear out the current selection.
2) It doesn't seem right to me that "Michael" should be interpreted the same in both departments. Do you know that selectInput options can have values that are distinct from labels? If the "choices" argument is a named list, the names are used as the display labels and the elements are what actually get passed back to server.R. So you could have employee IDs as the values and the employee names as the names.

messages.subject: Sankey networkD3 not working with rCharts
messages.subject_clean: Sankey networkD3 not working with rCharts
messages.body_plain:
First off, I have to say how much I love Shiny.  Thanks for building it and maintaining it so well!  Now on to my problem...

I can create either a Sankey plot from the networkD3 package, or an nPlot from rCharts, but not both.  Error message in the log of the browser says, "Uncaught TypeError: undefined is not a function".  The longer, more detailed description of the issue is at this link on stackoverflow <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/29056015/sankey-networkd3-not-working-with-rcharts>. Let me know if I should put all of that detail here too and I'll be happy to.

Here is my code for you to replicate at home.  Just comment out line 30, ",showOutput("plot_nvd3", "nvd3")" you'll see how the Sankey Plot starts to work.

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)
library(rCharts)
library(RCurl)
library(networkD3)

data(MisLinks)
data(MisNodes)

URL <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/christophergandrud/d3Network/sankey/JSONdata/energy.json"
Energy <- getURL(URL, ssl.verifypeer = FALSE)
EngLinks <- JSONtoDF(jsonStr = Energy, array = "links")
EngNodes <- JSONtoDF(jsonStr = Energy, array = "nodes")

ui <- dashboardPage(

  dashboardHeader(title = "Test"),
  dashboardSidebar(
    sidebarMenu(
      menuItem("A rChart Multibar", tabName = "rChart-multibar"),
      menuItem("B networkD3 Sankey", tabName = "networkD3-sankey"),
      menuItem("C networkD3 Force", tabName = "networkD3-force")
    )
  ),
  dashboardBody(
    tabItems(

      tabItem(tabName = "rChart-multibar", h2("A rChart")
              # comment out the following line, then the Sankey will work
              ,showOutput("plot_nvd3", "nvd3")
      ),

      tabItem(tabName = "networkD3-sankey",h2("B networkD3 Sankey")
              ,sankeyNetworkOutput("networkPlot")
      ),

      tabItem(tabName = "networkD3-force",h2("C networkD3 Force")
              ,forceNetworkOutput("force")
      )
    )

  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {

  output$plot_nvd3 = renderChart({

    ### Works in the browser, but not in the viewer window
    hair_eye_male <- subset(as.data.frame(HairEyeColor), Sex == "Male")
    nvd3_chart <- nPlot(Freq ~ Hair, group = "Eye", data = hair_eye_male,
                type = 'multiBarChart')
    nvd3_chart$addParams(width = 800, height = 400, dom = "plot_nvd3")
    return(nvd3_chart)

  })

  output$networkPlot <- renderSankeyNetwork({
    sankeyNetwork(Links = EngLinks, Nodes = EngNodes,
                  Source = "source", Target = "target",
                  Value = "value", NodeID = "name",
                  width = 700, fontsize = 12, nodeWidth = 30)
  })

  output$force <- renderForceNetwork({
    forceNetwork(Links = MisLinks, Nodes = MisNodes, Source = "source",
                 Target = "target", Value = "value", NodeID = "name",
                 Group = "group")
  })

}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Thanks!
Ben

messages.subject: Re: Icons in a datatable (DT)
messages.subject_clean: Icons in a datatable (DT)
messages.body_plain:
shiny::icon() uses the font-awesome library by default, and shiny does
not really know the dependency on font-awesome unless at least one
icon has been rendered in the shiny UI. In your case, you used
as.character(icon()), so shiny has no idea the app depends on
font-awesome (the dependency info is lost through as.character()). Two
possible solutions:

1. Render a hidden icon somewhere in your app, e.g.

fluidPage(
  ...,
  tags$span(icon(), style = "display: none;")
  ...
)

This will make shiny aware of the font-awesome dependency.

2. Use the glyphicon library instead, since it is shipped with
Bootstrap. You do not need to indicate a special dependency. See ?icon

Regards,
Yihui

I think this is happening because both networkD3 and rCharts are bringing in the d3 library, and they are conflicting.

We've created a standard way of incorporating JavaScript dependencies like this in the htmltools library; networkD3 uses this but rCharts does not. Ramnath, the author of rCharts, is working on an rCharts2 package that will use htmltools-based dependencies, which should fix this. (Or at least, get us to the next error message...)

messages.subject_clean: How to debug shinyapps.io hosted app
messages.body_plain:
Awesome! After debugging, I found out that shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> uses different locale settings, so when trying to do as.Date() using a short month name in the string (such as "Jan") did not work. I used the following inline code to convert my month name from my character data source to a number (where Month is the variable that has the value of the name you want to convert to a month index): match((Month),c("Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun","Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"))

Hope this might help someone in the future!

How are you supposed to debug an app that is hosted on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>? If it is failing, where do you look for errors?

Thanks for the advice! I have a follow-up question: do I really have to use as.character(icon(...)) if all I need is insert glyph(s) from font-awesome or glyphicon into my datatable? Is it possible to use <font...> or some class attribute in cells?

On Monday, March 23, 2015 at 5:55:58 PM UTC-5, Yihui Xie wrote:
> shiny::icon() uses the font-awesome library by default, and shiny does
> not really know the dependency on font-awesome unless at least one
> icon has been rendered in the shiny UI. In your case, you used
> as.character(icon()), so shiny has no idea the app depends on
> font-awesome (the dependency info is lost through as.character()). Two
> possible solutions:
>
> 1. Render a hidden icon somewhere in your app, e.g.
>
> fluidPage(
>   ...,
>   tags$span(icon(), style = "display: none;")
>   ...
> )
>
> This will make shiny aware of the font-awesome dependency.
>
> 2. Use the glyphicon library instead, since it is shipped with
> Bootstrap. You do not need to indicate a special dependency. See ?icon
>
> Regards,
> Yihui
>
>
> On Mon, Mar 23, 2015 at 4:29 PM, Alexander Vorobiev

I am building a shiny app which requires some data manipulation prior to display a chart.

below is my example, do you know how to solve this?

Thomas

  selectedAAA <- reactive({
                 dplot <- mydata %>%
                    filter(V1 %in% input$aaa, V2 %in% input$bbb) %>%
                    group_by(date, V1, V2)

                   spread(Material_Type, LT)
                 rownames(dplot) <- dplot$date
                dplot <- select(dplot, -c(Apigroup_Cd, date))
                dplot[is.na <http://is.na>(dplot)] <- 0

>> shiny::icon() uses the font-awesome library by default, and shiny does

>> icon has been rendered in the shiny UI. In your case, you used
>> as.character(icon()), so shiny has no idea the app depends on
>> font-awesome (the dependency info is lost through as.character()). Two
>> possible solutions:
>>
>> 1. Render a hidden icon somewhere in your app, e.g.
>>
>> fluidPage(
>>   ...,

>>   ...
>> )
>>

>>

>> Bootstrap. You do not need to indicate a special dependency. See ?icon

You should store the data frame using a reactiveValues object, and use an observeEvent to make the goButton trigger an edit.

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  v <- reactiveValues(data = data.frame(...))

  output$table <- renderTable({ v$data })

  observeEvent(input$goButton, {
    newpatientrow <- ...
    v$data <- rbind(v$data, newpatientrow)
  })
})

We'll have a new article on actionButton published on shiny.rstudio.com <http://shiny.rstudio.com> someday soon.

Are you saying that this doesn't run on Shiny Server? If you just log in with your regular SSH account and install, then you'll just be installing it in your own personal library.

Switch to either root:
sudo su -

or shiny:
sudo su - shiny

Then launch R and install the packages you want.

shinyUI(fluidPage(

                         choices = list("ODC" = "Direct New ODC", "ODO" = "Direct New ODO", "ODV" = "Direct New ODV","STD"="Direct New STD")

            hr(),
            radioButtons("segment", label = h4("FAP New"),
                         choices = list("EPQ" = "FAP New EPQ", "ODC" = "FAP New ODC")

                         choices = list("ODC" = "All Renew ODC", "ODO" = "All Renew ODO", "ODV" = "All Renew ODV","STD"="All Renew STD")),
)
)

messages.subject: Major shinyFiles update
messages.subject_clean: Major shinyFiles update
messages.body_plain:
I'm happy to announce that a major update to shinyFiles has just been send to CRAN and will likely become available within the next couple of days.

The update expands the server file system access by adding folder selection (much like choose.dir() on windows systems) and file saving dialog boxes.

With both folder selection and file saving it is possible to create new folders on the fly - shinyFiles monitors the permissions of the current location to make sure that write permissions are available.

With the file saver it is possible to specify different choices of filetypes - each filetype can contain multiple extensions (eg. jpg and jpeg).

messages.subject_clean: DataTable rows displayed through tabsetPanel
messages.body_plain:
hi Yihui,

actually I realize I prefer not to use DT until it is in CRAN, b/c of complications depending on a non-CRAN package.

however, i have made some progress with the classical dataTable, i think i'm close to the solution and i wanted to show you the approach in case you have some suggestion. i'm retrieving the current page for each tab via a callback function, so the only thing left would be how to tell renderDataTable() to show the dataTable at a specific page, here is a minimal example in which in one tab i show the first two columns of the iris data set and in a second tab the next three columns. at the bottom of each tab the current page saved via callback is shown. the goal is that when i switch tabs, i look to different columns of the same rows, i.e., i'm on the same page:

library(shiny)
shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(tabsetPanel(tabPanel("panel1", dataTableOutput('dt1'),
                                      verbatimTextOutput('infodt1'),
                                      value="p1"),
                             tabPanel("panel2", dataTableOutput('dt2'),
                                      verbatimTextOutput('infodt2'),
                                      value="p2"),
                             id="selpanel")),
  server = function(input, output) {

    output$dt1 = renderDataTable({ ## how can i show the page at input$page ?
      iris[, 1:2]
    }, callback = 'function(table) {
      table.on("draw", function() {
        Shiny.onInputChange("page", table.page <http://table.page>());
      });
    }')

    output$dt2 = renderDataTable({ ## how can i show the page at input$page ?
      iris[, 3:5]
    }, callback = 'function(table) {
      table.on("draw", function() {
        Shiny.onInputChange("page", table.page <http://table.page>());
      });
    }')

    output$infodt1 = renderPrint({
      input$page
    })

    output$infodt2 = renderPrint({
      input$page
    })
  }
)

thanks!!
robert.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server Question
messages.subject_clean: Shiny Server Question
messages.body_plain:
Hi there.

If you are behind a firewall or router and want to make it accessible from outside, you'll have to configure the firewall or router to do port forwarding of port 4949 to your own machine's IP address. You can run the linux command "ip addr" and find the "inet" field. If there are several, don't use the one that's 127.0.0.1.

Once you've done that (or you don't have a firewall/router) go to http://www.whatismyip.com or http://jsonip.com to see the IP address that your network presents to the outside world; that IP address should be the one you use from outside the network.

You might also have to allow port 4949 through on your software firewall--that is, the firewall software on your Linux box. If this is a fresh Ubuntu box then I highly recommend using the ufw package to manage your firewall; once ufw is installed and running I think it's just "ufw allow 4949", and maybe you have to do "ufw reload" after that. I think you can test if your software firewall will block requests by requesting http://ip-address-from-first-paragraph:4949, even from the same machine; if it succeeds, you're fine.

HTH,
-joe

messages.subject_clean: remove data file after plotting
messages.body_plain:
You probably don't want to delete it right after renderPlot; the plot will need to render again if the user resizes the browser window.

Add a "session" argument to your server function, i.e. "function(input, output, session)" then call something like this:

session$onSessionEnded(function() {
  if (!is.null(input$file1)) {
    file.remove(input$file1$datapath)
  }
})

though this will only delete the most recently uploaded file in this session, if any. If you want to delete more, keep a list of them as you go, and delete them all at the end.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

More experimenting with Shiny... I was willing to try the "single file" approach, as per
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/function.html

I have the following minimum function, borrowed from
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/tree/master/084-single-file

__________________________________________
shiny_test.r
------------------------
require("shiny")
# Global variables can go here
n <- 200
# Define the UI
ui <- bootstrapPage(
numericInput('n', 'Number of obs', n),
plotOutput('plot')
)
# Define the server code
server <- function(input, output) {
output$plot <- renderPlot({
hist(runif(input$n))
})
}
# Return a Shiny app object
cat("before\n")
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
cat("After\n")

------------------------------------------------------------------------

When I source the file (shiny_test.r), nothing happens. To me more specific -- "before" and "after" are printed all right, but the app does not start and that's all there is to say.

However, if (after having sourced the file once obviously) I copy the "shinyApp().." line and paste it into the console, the app starts alright in Firefox.

Any explanation/solution ?

Thanks

(R 3.1.3, Rgui 32 bits for Windows on a win7 machine)

messages.body_plain:
Oh sorry, I didn't see that you were sourcing the file. Normally we intend that you name the file app.R and call shiny::runApp(), passing it the directory in which app.R lives. This gives you the advantage of editing the app.R and hitting Reload in your browser without restarting Shiny.

If you really want to source it this way, put a print() or runApp() call around your shinyApp() call. That should launch it.

messages.subject: Re: Dataset filtering
messages.subject_clean: Dataset filtering
messages.body_plain:
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)

dataset <- ...

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("name", "Name", unique(dataset$names)),
  selectInput("year", "Year", unique(dataset$year)),
  textOutput("freq")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$freq <- renderText({
    # Make sure that name and year are selected
    validate(
      need(input$name, message = FALSE),
      need(input$year, message = FALSE)
    )

    dataset %>% filter(names == input$name & year == as.numeric(input$year))
  })
}

messages.body_plain:
A close() method would be great

On Tuesday, March 31, 2015, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> Just to be clear, stopApp() will stop the application for ALL connected users and exit the runApp() loop. It won't just terminate the session of the current user, if that's what you want.
>
> I guess we really ought to have a close() method on the session object <http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/session.html>...
>
> On Tue, Mar 31, 2015 at 3:16 PM, Jonah <jga...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > How exactly are you using stopApp()?
> >
> > If you use an actionButton then it will count for you and then you can use an observer to run stopApp() when the count is 20. In that context stopApp() should work.
> >
> > On Tuesday, March 31, 2015 at 12:37:11 PM UTC-4, Stéfane wrote:
> > > Hello,
> > >
> > > I'm using with a great pleasure the shiny extension in R. I've built a web application that shows an image pair. The application has a button to change the image pair. When the user clicks on it 20 times the application must stop. I try the function stopApp() but nothing happens. Do you know if there is a way to do it ?
